name: nav_entries
title: Navigation
description: One registry of the doors this server puts on itself. Before this collection there were THREE hand-maintained lists of the same apps and they had already drifted apart: a 25-entry JS array in site_nav's app switcher, a 21-entry Python tuple in site_home's tile grid, and a collection-to-URL map for search results -- each edited by whoever remembered, and between them naming none of the eight newest apps (shop, intake, billing, timers, banking, shipping, receiving, payments). A menu maintained by hand rots the moment somebody ships without editing it, and the rot is invisible: nothing fails, the front door simply advertises a server that no longer exists. So a package now DECLARES its doors in its manifest and install writes them here, the same way it declares its schedules. Every navigation surface becomes a fold over this one collection. The package owns label/path/blurb/group/surface/order and restates them on every install; the operator owns operator_hidden, which an install never writes -- the package says what an app IS, the operator says what they want to SEE.

fields.name: package
fields.label: Package
fields.help: Which package registered this door. Provenance, stamped by install: it is how a second package claiming the same path is caught, and how you find the manifest to edit when a label is wrong.

fields.name: path
fields.label: Path
fields.help: The URL this door opens, starting with '/'. Whether anything answers it is a routing question (convention, site_routes, or a views record) that this collection deliberately does not restate.

fields.name: blurb
fields.label: Blurb
fields.help: One honest line about what the app does. Shown under the label on the home grid.

fields.name: group
fields.label: Group
fields.help: Free text heading the entry sorts under: Work, Publishing, Money, Commerce, Warehouse, System. Free text rather than an enum so a new deployment can invent its own grouping without a schema migration.

fields.name: surface
fields.label: Surface
fields.help: Who this door is shown to: public (anyone, signed in or not), member (any signed-in user), operator (an admin role), hidden (registered but never rendered). This governs the MENU only -- it is not access control. Permissions decide who may actually open the page, and a surface of 'public' on a page the policy protects hides nothing that was not already protected.

fields.name: order
fields.label: Order
fields.help: Sort position within the group; ties break on label.

fields.name: operator_hidden
fields.label: Hidden by operator
fields.help: The operator's word, and install NEVER overwrites it. Set it to hide a door on this deployment without editing anybody's package; a reinstall or an upgrade restates label, path, blurb, group, order and surface but leaves this column exactly as you left it. Same posture as a paused schedule: the package declares what should be there, you decide what is there right now.
